entries.title: Jump to the brand kit from any surface it drives
entries.summary: A palette icon now appears next to every design surface that reads from a **Brand kit** — the event page builder, system email designer, title slide designer (**Colours** panel, next to **Reset to brand**), clip export editor (**Renders**), and the Create carousel toolbar (when a kit is selected). Clicking the icon opens the exact kit the design uses in a new tab, so unsaved work in the editor is not lost. Hovering or focusing the icon shows a tooltip listing which kit assets — logo, colour swatches, fonts, tagline, hashtags or clip caption style — that surface actually pulls from.
entries.use_case: When an organizer notices a colour or font looks off in a slide, clip or email design, they can click the palette icon to jump straight to the brand kit driving that design — without hunting through menus — and fix the source asset in one step.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all customers with Brand kit access (limited_release). No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep slides, clips and emails visually consistent, or when they struggle to find which kit is driving a particular design.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Brand kits with Slides, Clips, or Create carousels.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Brand → any kit; or open a slide/clip/carousel/page-builder design and look for the palette icon
internal.gotchas: The link is intentionally absent from booklets, Advocacy Quick Launch and Advocacy video templates — those surfaces do not read the Marketing brand kit, so the link would point at irrelevant assets. Webinar share cards and email signatures are also not yet wired (coming in a follow-up branch).
internal.talk_track: Every design surface that uses your brand kit now has a palette icon that takes you straight to that kit in a new tab — so you can check or update the source without losing your place in the editor.

draft.docs_gap: The brand-kits guide should add a section listing every surface that displays the palette shortcut icon and explaining that the tooltip shows which specific kit assets (logo, colours, fonts, voice, clips) that surface reads.
draft.why_use_it: Brand kits let you define your event's logo, colours, fonts, voice and content rules in one place so every marketing surface — slides, clips, carousels, page builder and system emails — stays visually consistent without manual updates. When a kit changes, every surface that reads from it reflects the update automatically. Use a brand kit whenever you want a team of contributors to produce on-brand content without coordinating design decisions individually.

entries.title: Create credits quotes to the person who said them
entries.summary: Drafts in **Create** now credit quotes and paraphrases to the participant tagged on that part of the transcript — "Name, Job Title, Company" by default — instead of "one speaker". Hover a citation to see who said it, their session role and the timestamp; citations from untagged parts of the transcript are flagged so you can tag the speaker and **Redraft**. **Settings → Speaker credit** chooses the format, and **Copilot** can answer "who said this?" and fix attributions using the same data.

where.path: Marketing → Create → a project → Settings → Speaker credit

entries.use_case: When a marketer drafts a one-pager or blog from a session, the quotes come out credited to the real speaker — name, title and company — instead of "one panelist said", so the draft is ready to publish without a round of copy-pasting speaker details.

cs_action.note: On for every Create user. Attribution follows the transcript speaker tags, so a draft is only as good as the tagging.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains that Create drafts say "a speaker" or that Copilot asks them to paste a speaker's name (SB-10990, Clarion).
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Live Transcribe or Media transcripts with Create.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Create → open a project with a tagged session in Sources → Redraft, then hover a citation
internal.gotchas: Untagged transcript passages stay generic by design. Participants whose seat on the session is hidden are never named. Old drafts keep their old citations until Redraft.
internal.talk_track: Create now knows who said what. Tag speakers in the transcript once and every draft credits them by name, title and company.
